problem: Existing VLA models are trained on terrestrial, mostly 2D planar data and fail on underwater robots with 3D thruster-based motion and strong visual domain shift; underwater datasets are perception/SLAM-only with no language or action labels, and real data collection is costly.
motivation: Underwater missions need multi-task autonomy (navigation, manipulation, tracking) with minimal human intervention, but work is fragmented into task-specific expert models. A simulated, language-annotated multi-task dataset plus a VLA model with better spatial awareness could provide a general-purpose foundation.
key_idea: Build a large automated simulation dataset (USIM) for BlueROV2 with a unified thruster+arm action space, and train a GR00T N1.5-based VLA (U0) with a conv-attention CAP module that predicts the 6-DoF target pose as an auxiliary task.
insight: Fine-tuning on USIM cuts offline APE for all baselines by ~59.7% on average and lifts online SR from near zero to non-trivial, so the data itself is the main enabler of underwater transfer. The auxiliary CAP pose-prediction adds a further gain: ablation w/o CAP gives 35.6% overall SR vs 43.1% with it, with large gains on some tasks (Goto charge station 72.5%→97.5%, Scan ship Ancient 40%→90%) but neutral or negative on others (e.g. Scan ship Modern 95%→85%), so the gain is uneven.
method: USIM data synthesis: Stonefish simulator with 9 scenarios, BlueROV2 with optional 4-DoF arm and gripper, ROS-based collection; scene/lighting/object randomization; hand-crafted expert policies using GT sim state with stochastic noise injection to capture sub-optimal states and recovery behaviors
USIM contents: 905K frames, 2275 trajectories, ~25 h at 10 Hz, 20 tasks (12 grasping, 6 navigation, 1 tracking, 1 transport) with language instructions
Unified state/action space: two RGB views + IMU, DVL, depth, thruster commands and arm joint states as state; normalized thruster PWM concatenated with arm joint positions as action
U0 backbone: initialized from Isaac-GR00T N1.5 (3B); VLM encodes images+language to 2048-d, sensors via MLP, DiT action head with flow matching generating H=16 action chunks, K=4 Euler steps

CAP module: conv layers with padding mask, conv-based channel attention, pooling and MLP on VLM features to predict a 6-DoF target pose (object/waypoint/tracked target) in robot-centric frame; loss L = L_action + 1.0·L_CAP
Evaluation framework: offline APE (MSE) on 525 test trajectories, and automated online closed-loop sim eval with SR, SSR, SPL, ASD, MTD over 700 trials on 20 tasks

setting.backbone: GR00T N1.5-initialized VLA with DiT action head + CAP module (fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: USIM train split: 77% (697K frames) of 905K simulated frames, 20 tasks; expert-generated
setting.observation: Dual RGB cameras + IMU + DVL + pressure depth + thruster commands + arm joint states + language instruction
setting.action_space: Low-level unified continuous action: normalized thruster PWM intensities + arm joint positions, 16-step chunks at 10 Hz
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT sim state used only by expert policies for data collection and CAP pose supervision in training)

numbers.extra: fine-tuned on USIM; 700 online trials across 20 tasks in Stonefish
numbers.evidence: Table online_cmp: U0 Navigation SR 87.5% SPL 0.71±0.23

numbers.extra: fine-tuned on USIM; 700 trials; grasp SR 30.0%, ASD 87.6 s; transport SR 25.0%, SSR 45.0%; tracking SR 40.0%, MTD 3.61 m

numbers_note: Custom USIM benchmark, no standard navigation benchmarks; the w/o-CAP overall SR equals the GR00T N1.5 baseline's 35.6% (249/700) as printed.
results: U0 achieves the lowest offline APE (0.0359 vs GR00T N1.5 0.0374) and the best online overall SR of 43.1% vs π0.5 at 37.6% and GR00T N1.5 at 35.6%; navigation reaches 87.5% SR. Zero-shot terrestrial VLAs fail; OpenVLA gets 0% grasp/transport, and π0.5 remains best on grasping SR (37.1% vs U0 30.0%).
limitations: Simulation only; no real-world deployment or sim-to-real validation, vision only without sonar for low visibility
Absolute manipulation success remains low (grasp 30%, transport 25%) and grasps take ~2x the expert's time; CAP gains are inconsistent across tasks
Train and test share the same scenes and distribution, so generalization to unseen environments is not tested; expert data relies on GT sim state
